narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Three divisions in a row will leave something smaller than ten.
<bookmark mark='size'/>Dividing by all three is dividing once by seven times eleven times thirteen. That is about one thousand.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>A six digit number divided by about one thousand keeps three digits. That guess is far too small.
removed_beats.on_screen: the hint card leaves; Chintu's bubble shows smaller than 10; 7 × 11 × 13 is written and grows to about one thousand; the bubble is struck in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='own'/>To check, pick another three digit number and repeat its digits.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Or multiply your number by seven, eleven and thirteen. You should see it written twice.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor and the answer card; two check lines appear: pick another three digit number; multiply back by 7, 11 and 13

old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu thinks three divisions must leave something smaller than ten. Seven times eleven times thirteen is only about one thousand, so a six digit number shrinks to a three digit one.
